test_title: RRB NTPC Graduate Level CBT-I Official Paper (Held On: 20 Jun, 2025 Shift 2)
subject: general
question: In △ABC, DE ∥ AC, where D and E are the points on sides AB and BC, respectively.If BD = 12 cm and AD = 11 cm, then what is the ratio of the area of △BDE to that of the trapezium ADEC?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Side ratio of **ΔBDE** to **ΔBAC** = BD : (BD + AD) = 12 : (12 + 11) = 12 : 23.

Area ratio of **ΔBDE** to **ΔBAC** = 12² : 23² = 144 : 529.

Area of **trapezium ADEC** = Area(ΔBAC) − Area(ΔBDE) = 529 − 144 = 385 units.

Required ratio = Area(ΔBDE) : Area(trapezium ADEC) = 144 : 385.

**∴ The correct answer is 144 : 385.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

In **ΔABC**, **DE || AC**. **BD** = 12 cm and **AD** = 11 cm.

**Formula Used:**

If two triangles are **similar**, the ratio of their **areas** is equal to the **square** of the ratio of their **corresponding sides**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/bb3984156afea3706e6941d1f2ad403014c467054db8841c9f8f329090d00e75.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Total length of side **AB** = **BD** + **AD**

⇒ **AB** = 12 + 11 = 23 cm

⇒ Since **DE || AC**, **ΔBDE ∼ ΔBAC** (by **AA similarity** criterion)

⇒ Area(ΔBDE) ÷ Area(ΔBAC) = (BD ÷ AB)²

⇒ Area(ΔBDE) ÷ Area(ΔBAC) = (12 ÷ 23)² = 144 ÷ 529

⇒ Let Area(ΔBDE) = 144 units and Area(ΔBAC) = 529 units

⇒ Area(trapezium ADEC) = Area(ΔBAC) − Area(ΔBDE)

⇒ Area(trapezium ADEC) = 529 − 144 = 385 units

⇒ Ratio = Area(ΔBDE) : Area(trapezium ADEC) = 144 : 385

**∴ The correct answer is 144 : 385.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Basic Proportionality Theorem (Thales Theorem)

If a line is drawn parallel to one side of a triangle, it divides the other two sides in the same ratio: BD/AD = BE/EC.

Area of Similar Triangles

The ratio of the areas of two similar triangles is equal to the square of the ratio of any two corresponding sides: Area1/Area2 = (s1/s2)².

AA Similarity Criterion

If two angles of one triangle are equal to two angles of another triangle, then the two triangles are similar.</p
